note: Expected verdicts for the action-ref-v2 conformance vectors. v2 preimage and field set are IDENTICAL to v1 -- {action_type, agent_id, scope, timestamp}, same JCS canonicalization -- only a fixed domain tag ('mycelium.action-ref:v2:') is prepended to the canonical JSON bytes before hashing, and the resulting hex digest is prefixed 'v2:'. This is ADDITIVE to the v1 profile (see ../manifest/), not a replacement: v1 hashes remain permanently valid and are never retroactively invalidated. A conformant v2 verifier MUST reproduce PASS on positives (byte-identical v1 and v2 digest, non-colliding) and MUST reproduce REJECT on negatives, each exercising a distinct way domain separation can be broken or bypassed -- see reject_reasons and verify.py.

reject_reasons.cross_protocol_collision_risk: a bare, untagged 64-hex digest (indistinguishable from any other bare-SHA-256(JCS(4-field-object)) scheme) is presented as satisfying the v2 profile -- exactly the collision class the v1->v2 split exists to close, documented in RFC 002
reject_reasons.wrong_domain_tag: the claimed v2 value was computed under a domain tag other than the one this spec defines ('mycelium.action-ref:v2:') -- a generic or differently-scoped tag does not close cross-protocol collision, it just moves the collision surface to the tag namespace itself
reject_reasons.tag_applied_post_hash: the claimed v2 value hashes the domain tag together with an already-computed v1 digest's hex string, instead of prepending the tag to the canonical preimage bytes before hashing once -- defeats domain separation by leaving a bare, undomain-separated hash one layer underneath
